verdicts.reason: A clips the NEW pill against the left edge and stacks it on top of the bottle. The cream circle is cut off at the bottom-left, and the headline wraps into two cramped lines. B is basically a shrunk copy of the original with the bottle circle slightly clipped at the bottom and a tiny NEW label, but its order (brand, headline, badge, CTA) is clean and everything is readable.

A keeps the original's left-to-right order, but it is a straight shrink: the bottle circle is clipped at the bottom and the NEW text is tiny. B reverses the reading order by putting the CTA first, makes the Try It button tiny and hard to read, and lets the NEW badge collide with the bottle at the far right, so the brand image ends up as an afterthought.
